# Creating a command

Commands are declared with `defineCommand`, `defineOption` and `defineArgument`, on top of `cliparse`. Options and arguments are validated and parsed by [Zod](https://zod.dev) schemas, and their types flow into the handler. The reasons behind this design are explained in [ADR 0001](../adr/adr-0001-rework-file-structure.md).

Before writing a command, look at a similar one and copy its naming, file layout, output format and error messages. `src/commands/drain/` is a good example of a command group with shared arguments and options.

## Example

A fictional `clever coffee brew <blend>` subcommand, part of a `coffee` group (neither exists in the CLI). The `<blend>` argument is shared by several `coffee` subcommands, so it lives in `coffee.args.js`:

```js
// src/commands/coffee/coffee.args.js
import { z } from 'zod';
import { defineArgument } from '../../lib/define-argument.js';

export const blendArg = defineArgument({
  schema: z.string().regex(/^[a-z0-9-]+$/, 'Use lowercase letters, digits and dashes'),
  description: 'Blend of coffee',
  placeholder: 'blend',
});
```

I added the `clever oauth-consumers` group, but I haven't run any subcommand against the API. The API paths, the request body shape and the Console URL below are from memory, so they need checking. `npm run validate` passes (lint, format, types, docs), and `node bin/clever.js oauth-consumers --help` lists all the subcommands.

- **`clever oauth-consumers`** lists consumers, with `--format json` available.
- **`get <consumer-key>`** shows one consumer. `--with-secret` also prints the secret, and it needs the same care as `clever oauth-consumers get --with-secret` in AGENTS.md.
- **`create <name>`** takes `--description`, `--url`, `--base-url`, `--picture` and `--rights a,b`.
- **`update <consumer-key>`** takes the same flags plus `--name`.
  - It errors if you pass none of them.
  - It reads the current consumer first and sends the whole thing back, on the assumption that the API replaces it.
- **`delete <consumer-key>`** asks for confirmation unless you pass `--yes`.
- **`open <consumer-key>`** opens the consumer in the Console.
- Every subcommand takes `--org`, so you can target an organisation; the default is your own account.

The generated docs (`src/commands/README.md` and the skill's full documentation) are updated. The new commands use `since: null`.

**To verify:**
- **API paths:** I wrote the endpoints in `src/clever-client/oauth-consumers.js` against `/v2/organisations/{id}/consumers[/{key}]`. `node_modules` wasn't installed at the start, so I couldn't see whether `@clevercloud/client` already has them.
- **Console URL:** `open` uses `/organisations/{id}/oauth-consumers/{key}`, which I guessed. Please confirm the real Console route.
- **Rights names:** `--rights` accepts any string and sends each one as `true`. I didn't check the names against the API.

I haven't committed anything. Running prettier changed `.claude/settings.json`, so I reverted that file.
